ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The expression denotes the whole body is eyes in these Chan records. Its wording is 'the whole body is eyes.
EvidenceBody: Chan records make the whole body an organ of seeing, commonly beside whole-body hearing, speaking, or acting. Yuanwu says, 'the whole body is eyes, yet seeing does not reach it,' and extends the same construction to ears, mouth, and mind. Another discourse pairs 'the whole body is a mouth' with 'the whole body is eyes,' then assigns the former speech and the latter use. In public questioning, 'the Great Compassionate One does not extend a hand; the whole body is eyes' answers the class 'meaning and phrase both arrive.' Later case comments use the phrase as an appraisal of Yuanwu Keqin and as wording that itself still requires investigation.
